# Lab 6 — A graph without references between nodes

**Unit:** [week 6, memory safety II: borrowing](../../week06-borrowing.md)
(exercises 1 and 3). **Time:** 2 hours. **Runs in the playground:** yes
(the solution runs there; the starter's borrow error comes from `fid`, so
run `fid check` for task 1).

References are second-class in Fid: they cannot be stored in a struct or a
`Vec`. A graph therefore keeps its edges as indexes. You meet the borrow
checker's rule against two mutable borrows of one value, then write a
depth-first search over indexes.

## Start

- [Open the starter in the playground](https://fides-lang.org/playground#) to read it, and
- copy [`starter.fd`](starter.fd) and run `fid check starter.fd`. It is
  rejected.

Embed:

## Tasks

1. **Read the error.** The self-loop `link(&mut d, &mut d, 3, 3)` takes two
   mutable borrows of `d` at once. Replace `link` by
   `add_edge(g: &mut Graph, x: i64, y: i64)`: read the node out of
   `g.nodes`, push the edge, store it back. Make sure `x == y` works.
2. **Depth-first search.** Write
   `dfs(g: &Graph, start: i64, seen: &mut Vec<bool>) -> Vec<i64>` with an
   explicit stack (no recursion), visiting lower indexes first.
3. **Components.** Build the graph a–b, b–d, d–d, a–c, c–d, e–f with
   `add_node` and `add_edge`. Print the order from `a`, then run `dfs` from
   every node not yet seen, print each further component, and print the
   number of components.

## Check your work

When you are done, `fid run starter.fd` prints:

```text
6 nodes
from a: a b d c
another component: e f
2 components
```

## Questions to hand in

- Why does `add_edge` work for `x == y` when `link` could not? What does
  `g.nodes.get(x)` give you: a reference or a value?
- Storing a node back after each change copies its edge list. Propose a
  layout (for example one `Vec<i64>` of edges for the whole graph) that
  avoids it, and say what it costs.

## For instructors

[`solution.fd`](solution.fd) is a model answer and
[`expected.txt`](expected.txt) what it prints;
`python3 tests/course/check_labs.py --fid <fid> lab06` checks both. A
borrow-checker gap worth showing (Nov 17): holding
`val ns: &mut Vec<Node> = &mut g.nodes;` across a call that reads `&g`,
then using `ns` again, is accepted.
